name: Technogaianism
summary: Technogaianism is a bright green, transhumanist-flavoured environmentalism that holds emerging technologies (clean energy, biotechnology, nanotechnology, geoengineering, space-based monitoring) can heal the Earth and restore ecosystems rather than harm them. It rejects the radical-green view that technology inherently degrades nature, and treats resource exhaustion as a civilisational threat. It has no worked-out economic or constitutional programme, so most political questions beyond technology and environment are left open.
scope: The bright green technogaian strand as described in Wikipedia's Technogaianism article (George Dvorsky, James Hughes, Walter Truett Anderson, Michael Rosenzweig, S. Matthew Liao) and the adjacent Viridian design movement of Bruce Sterling. Used with bright green environmentalism and ecomodernism for positions on nuclear power, GM crops and cities. Excludes dark-green, degrowth and primitivist environmentalism.

furtherReading.title: Bright green environmentalism (Wikipedia)
furtherReading.note: The wider current technogaianism belongs to, contrasted with light and dark greens.

furtherReading.title: Viridian Manifesto (Bruce Sterling)
furtherReading.note: A founding text of the Viridian design movement, arguing for glamorous, design-led climate action.

furtherReading.title: Ecomodernism (Wikipedia)
furtherReading.note: A neighbouring pro-technology environmental outlook, with its stance on nuclear, GM crops and decoupling.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; a democratic-transhumanist, Hughes-style outlook that wants broad access to biotechnology implies support for public provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is outside the movement's concerns, and the Viridian texts focus on design and culture, so adherents have no common line.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sterling dismisses industry as too short-sighted to see planetary survival as profit while also rejecting dirigiste rationing, so adherents split.

public-ownership.rationale: The sources say nothing on ownership; Viridian doubts industry and governments alike, leaving no settled view.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Economic distribution is not addressed in the technogaian literature, so no common position can be shown.

unions-good.rationale: Labor organisation is never discussed; the movement is silent and adherents' views follow their wider politics.

property-fundamental.rationale: Environmental goals such as resource limits and environmental crime tribunals imply property should yield to ecological protection.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Sterling expects industry to resist regulation but also says governments lack the will for top-down solutions, so the sources do not favour tighter rules as such.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; a humanist, democratic-transhumanist outlook is unlikely to see welfare as harmful dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Business ownership forms are not discussed by the movement.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; transhumanist civil-liberties leanings suggest scepticism of surveillance, though the sources do not say.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is not part of the technogaian texts, and adherents differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech law is not addressed and adherents' views follow their general politics.

strong-leader.rationale: Hughes-style democratic transhumanism argues democratic societies must respond to technology, which implies opposition to bypassing democratic process.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement seeks civilisation-scale environmental repair and democratic governance of technology, which presupposes functioning institutions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's concerns are environmental and technological, with no call for more coercive capacity.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; adherents follow general liberal or conservative leanings.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; a humanist, science-minded outlook typically favours rehabilitation, inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Transhumanist enhancement ideas and a future-oriented outlook sit poorly with defending traditional structures as society's foundation; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; the democratic-transhumanist milieu around Hughes and Dvorsky is socially liberal, inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; bodily-autonomy leanings of the transhumanist milieu suggest support, inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Technogaianism grounds itself in science and technology rather than faith, though its Gaian name is spiritual in origin; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian democratic-transhumanist milieu.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement is global and planetary in outlook but does not address national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Sterling's manifesto calls for a rapid new culture of design and technology, not respect for established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; the planetary, cosmopolitan framing suggests opposition, inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sterling doubts national governments can act but does not endorse international bodies; planetary problems might favour them, so split.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is outside the sources, which only discuss technology and environment; adherents hold no shared view.

nation-first.rationale: Environmental repair is framed as a global problem for the whole Earth, which cuts against national priority; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Military intervention is never discussed by technogaian writers, so there is no shared position.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; cosmopolitan leanings are offset by the lack of any stated position.

limit-growth.rationale: Bright green thinking holds that prosperity can keep growing while ecological footprints shrink, rejecting the degrowth of dark greens.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Technogaians hold civilisation faces mass extinction unless damage is mitigated, and endorse geoengineering and clean technology, though mainly via technology rather than state commands.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The core claim is that technology can reverse environmental degradation, though the sources frame this as environmental problems rather than all of humanity's.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Wikipedia lists nuclear power among technological mitigations technogaians endorse, and ecomodernists treat it as acceptable where net impact is lower.

revolution-justified.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's change comes through design and technology rather than politics.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hughes and others stress democratic response to technology, while the movement relies on scientists and engineers; adherents split.

central-planning.rationale: Sterling states national governments lack power and will for dirigiste solutions and rejects top-down rationing.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is not mentioned in the technogaian or Viridian texts.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Estate taxation is not a technogaian topic; no source states a position.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; some transhumanists support it, the sources do not.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; protecting incumbent industry sits poorly with a movement based on technological change, inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Ecomodernists call for state investment in technology but others in the family favour design and culture over government; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nothing in the movement envisions abolishing money; its programme works within existing economies through new technology.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; state-run wage bodies have no place in the movement's technology-and-design programme.

one-party-rule.rationale: Democratic transhumanist strands such as Hughes's argue democracies must govern technology, which excludes single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; a modernist, democratic outlook suggests rejection.

democracy-best.rationale: Hughes and Anderson, cited in the Wikipedia article, argue democratic societies should shape technological change, supporting democracy though 'even when voters choose badly' is untested.

direct-votes.rationale: The sources favour democratic response to technology but never mention referendums or direct legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: Not addressed; no council-based politics appears in the movement.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is not discussed; the movement's concern is planetary rather than territorial.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; an egalitarian democratic-transhumanist outlook implies rejection.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no stated line.

war-builds-character.rationale: The movement is oriented to healing Earth and avoiding catastrophe, which is at odds with glorifying war; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; the science-based, secular tone of the transhumanist milieu suggests support, inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The movement rests on science and technology, with no scriptural basis for law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a democratic-governance outlook.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; planetary concerns are non-military, inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not addressed; the planetary, universalist framing rules out ethnic nationhood, inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Sterling frames the central issue as technocultural, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distributive egalitarianism is not part of the technogaian literature, so adherents split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land rights are not discussed in the sources, though ecological sympathies might cut either way.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are not a technogaian topic and no source addresses them.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; planetary framing is global rather than civilisational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ethical egoism is not discussed; the movement stresses duties to the planet, but also market-friendly design incentives.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; transhumanist emphasis on individual freedom to enhance suggests rights priority, inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Technogaians aim to heal Earth and maintain ecologically diverse habitats, which presupposes value in ecosystems; Dvorsky's animal-rights stance supports it, though it is not stated as a philosophical claim.

limit-population.rationale: Population is not addressed in the Wikipedia article; Liao's proposal to engineer humans works on per-person impact instead.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Technogaianism is defined against radical environmentalists who hold all technology degrades the environment; it sees technology as becoming cleaner and a means of repair.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The movement wants emerging technologies developed and deployed quickly to repair the environment, and Hughes argues societies must adapt to change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Liao's proposal to engineer humans and the transhumanist origin of the movement support freedom to enhance, though the freedom framing is inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; adherents may be open to it but sources say nothing.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the transhumanist, civil-liberties-minded milieu.

restore-past-order.rationale: Sterling's manifesto demands a new, 'unnatural' and mediated green rather than any return to a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Bright greens emphasise tools, models and ideas that work over limits and ideology, though the statement is not stated as such.

direct-action.rationale: Sterling's route is design and culture to create demand, and bright greens say society cannot protest its way to sustainability.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative politics is not discussed; Sterling's design-led method is instrumental rather than prefigurative, but nothing is stated.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement contrasts itself with radical environmentalists and seeks sustainable technology plus restored ecosystems, not abandoning civilisation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; technological specialisation is assumed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution principles are never addressed by technogaian authors.

production-for-use.rationale: The movement says nothing on profit versus use as the purpose of production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Sterling sees industry as short-sighted rather than exploitative and does not adopt a labor-exploitation theory; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Not addressed; incompatible with a democratic-governance outlook.

collective-farming.rationale: Ecomodernist-style high-tech agriculture is not collectivist, and the sources never discuss collectives; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; not part of the movement's analysis.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; funding environmental repair and public goods implies taxation is legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; liberal transhumanist leanings suggest support, inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights theory is not discussed; the sources do not say whether groups hold rights.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal and anti-militarist leanings.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Hughes-style democratic participation is favoured over exit, inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic orientation.

positive-liberty.rationale: The sources do not engage with theories of freedom, so no position can be stated.

media-academia-power.rationale: Technogaian authors do not discuss where political power lies in media or universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; contrary to the humanist egalitarian outlook, inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic orientation.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; rebirth is framed as planetary and technological, not national.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; expansion appears only as space expansion, not state aggrandisement.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; incompatible with a modernist outlook.

bound-labor.rationale: Not addressed; incompatible with any liberal or transhumanist outlook.

universal-morality.rationale: Metaethics is outside the sources; the transhumanist and Gaian strands might answer differently.

single-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; pluralist democratic orientation suggests rejection, inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not a technogaian concern.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not discussed by the movement.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporate governance is not addressed by technogaian or Viridian sources.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not discussed by the movement.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is outside the sources, which concentrate on technology and environment.

economic-freedom.rationale: The sources do not link political freedom to economic freedom either way.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a global-problems, cooperative outlook.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; cosmopolitan outlook suggests opposition, inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not part of the technogaian literature.

class-collaboration.rationale: Employer-worker relations are not discussed by the movement.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Sterling's manifesto contrasts real culture with the culture industry and wants new design, but does not call for destroying inherited institutions; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; inconsistent with a global cooperative framing.

workers-nation.rationale: Working-class organisation is not discussed; the movement's global framing weighs lightly against national lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; contrary to the progressive transhumanist milieu, inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; no sign the movement opposes finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed; contrary to universalist humanist values, inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Technogaianism seeks cleaner and alternative technologies and mitigating resource exhaustion; Sterling also treats climate as the central design problem.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigrant integration is not discussed by the movement.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed; a conspiracy view with no basis in the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the sources.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; no national mission appears in a planetary movement.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender structure is not addressed by technogaian authors.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Sterling calls governments weak and industry stupid, but not specifically corrupt.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The movement includes genetic engineering but frames it as individual choice and environmental impact reduction (Liao), not state coercion; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional justice is not a technogaian topic.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement wants environmental protection and crime tribunals, exceeding a minimal state, though Sterling doubts national governments' capacity.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed; contrary to the movement's universalist outlook, inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from democratic transhumanism and Dvorsky's wider rights concerns.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Debates on socialist strategy are irrelevant to the movement and never mentioned.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is not discussed by technogaian sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal law is not discussed in the movement's texts.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; a liberal outlook suggests opposition.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; Dvorsky is a vegetarian but the movement has no position on bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a secular, science-based outlook.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist state theory is irrelevant to the movement and unaddressed.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Not addressed explicitly; implied by the democratic outlook of Hughes and Anderson.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balances are not a technogaian concern.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no stated line.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Sources credit technology and design with driving progress but never frame struggle between peoples as its engine.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed; contrary to a humanist outlook.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are not discussed by technogaian authors.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not engaged by the sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; democratic governance of technology implies checks, inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not addressed; contrary to a democratic outlook.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Distributive priorities are not addressed in the sources.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not discussed by the movement.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor law is not discussed in the technogaian literature.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses technological solutions rather than blaming population; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in the sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from civil-libertarian leanings.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not discussed; Sterling rejects rationing, but this is a different issue.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; contrary to democratic outlook.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions are not discussed in the sources.

notes: Technogaianism is a thin ideology politically: only technology, environment and enhancement answers are medium confidence; nearly everything else is inferred from the democratic-transhumanist and bright green milieu. Strands differ on state role (Hughes favours democratic governance, Sterling doubts governments) and on markets.
